books.title: I'll Give You the Sun
books.author: Jandy Nelson
books.ratingNote: Consistently high reader ratings across platforms.
reviewSummary: Told in dual timelines from the perspectives of twins Jude and Noah, this novel explores grief, betrayal, art, and first love. Readers frequently praise the lyrical writing and emotional ambition, especially how the shifting structure slowly reveals misunderstandings that tore the siblings apart. Reviews often highlight how art becomes both refuge and language for pain. Many readers describe the book as overwhelming in the best way and deeply cathartic.

books.title: The Sky Is Everywhere
books.author: Jandy Nelson
books.ratingNote: Strong long-term reader reception.
reviewSummary: After her sister’s sudden death, Lennie struggles to move through grief while caught between two very different boys. Readers praise how the novel portrays mourning as messy and intrusive rather than linear. Reviews often note the way poetry and music function as emotional survival tools. Many describe the book as romantic, painful, and emotionally immersive.

books.title: When the World Tips Over
books.author: Jandy Nelson
books.ratingNote: Positive reception with praise for scope and ambition.
reviewSummary: A multigenerational family story blending realism with magical elements as siblings confront addiction, disappearance, and inherited trauma. Readers praise the emotional density and interconnected narratives, though some note the complexity demands attention. Reviews highlight themes of forgiveness and how family damage echoes over time. Many describe it as lush and emotionally demanding.

books.title: The Authentics
books.author: Abdi Nazemian
books.ratingNote: Strong engagement from identity-focused YA readers.
reviewSummary: An Iranian American teen navigates friendship fractures, cultural identity, and family secrets after uncovering truths about her past. Readers praise the humor and cultural specificity, noting how identity is portrayed as layered rather than fixed. Reviews often highlight the tension between assimilation and authenticity. Many describe it as insightful and emotionally honest.

books.title: Don't Hate the Player
books.author: Alexis Nedd
books.ratingNote: Solid ratings with appeal to gaming and competition fans.
reviewSummary: A competitive gamer balances esports, student politics, and friendship pressures as her secret hobby collides with public expectations. Readers appreciate the insider look at gaming culture. Reviews often highlight themes of ambition and gender assumptions. Many describe it as fast-paced and relatable.

books.title: Different for Boys
books.author: Patrick Ness
books.ratingNote: Praised for honesty and formal experimentation.
reviewSummary: Told with humor and visual redactions, the novel explores teen sexuality, masculinity, and emotional confusion. Readers praise the candid tone and structural creativity. Reviews often highlight how vulnerability and loneliness are centered rather than labels. Many describe it as funny, painful, and refreshingly direct.

books.title: Yours from the Tower
books.author: Sally Nicholls
books.ratingNote: Positive reception among historical fiction readers.
reviewSummary: An epistolary novel following three friends navigating love, class, and ambition in late-19th-century England. Readers praise the witty letters and Austen-inspired tone. Reviews often mention how female friendship anchors the story. Many describe it as charming and comforting.

books.title: We Are All Made of Molecules
books.author: Susin Nielsen
books.ratingNote: Strong reader love driven by humor and heart.
reviewSummary: Two teens with clashing personalities are forced into a blended family while dealing with grief and social pressure. Readers praise the alternating perspectives and sharp humor. Reviews highlight how comedy softens heavy topics without dismissing them. Many describe it as laugh-out-loud and deeply kind.

books.title: This Is Where It Ends
books.author: Marieke Nijkamp
books.ratingNote: High engagement with intense reader reactions.
reviewSummary: Told over 54 minutes during a school shooting, the novel alternates between multiple student perspectives. Readers praise the immediacy and emotional urgency. Reviews often note how the structure amplifies tension and helplessness. Many describe it as harrowing but impactful.

books.title: All the Bright Places
books.author: Jennifer Niven
books.ratingNote: Extremely large readership with lasting popularity.
reviewSummary: A love story between two teens coping with grief and mental illness. Readers praise the emotional intimacy and road-trip structure. Reviews often note its impact while also acknowledging its heaviness. Many describe it as heartbreaking and memorable.

books.title: Holding Up the Universe
books.author: Jennifer Niven
books.ratingNote: Strong reader engagement driven by emotional connection.
reviewSummary: Two teens, both misjudged by their peers, form a bond while navigating grief, body image, and neurological difference. Readers praise the empathy-centered storytelling and dual perspectives. Reviews often highlight the focus on truly seeing others beyond labels. Many describe it as hopeful and emotionally affirming.

books.title: When We Ride
books.author: Rex Ogle
books.ratingNote: Positive response to its verse format and intensity.
reviewSummary: Written in verse, the novel follows two boys whose loyalty is tested as violence and drugs close in around them. Readers praise the urgency and emotional compression of the poetry. Reviews often mention how quickly tension escalates. Many describe it as raw and unsettling.

books.title: ASAP
books.author: Axie Oh
books.ratingNote: Generally positive reception among romance readers.
reviewSummary: A contemporary romance exploring ambition, timing, and emotional vulnerability. Readers praise the fast pacing and character chemistry. Reviews often highlight themes of pressure and self-definition. Many describe it as engaging and heartfelt.

books.title: XOXO
books.author: Axie Oh
books.ratingNote: Strong popularity driven by K-pop–themed romance.
reviewSummary: A forbidden romance between a classical musician and a K-pop idol navigating fame and secrecy. Readers praise the glamorous setting and emotional tension. Reviews often highlight the balance between dreams and relationships. Many describe it as escapist and sweet.

books.title: Consent
books.author: Nancy Ohlin
books.ratingNote: Divided but intense reader reactions.
reviewSummary: A student-teacher relationship is slowly reframed as manipulation rather than romance. Readers praise the psychological tension while noting the discomfort is intentional. Reviews often highlight the shifting power dynamics and unreliable narration. Many describe it as disturbing but thought-provoking.

books.title: Lycanthropy and Other Chronic Illnesses
books.author: Kristen O'Neal
books.ratingNote: Strong response from chronic illness representation readers.
reviewSummary: A teen coping with Lyme disease finds connection through an online support group that may not be entirely human. Readers praise the metaphor-driven approach to chronic illness. Reviews often highlight humor blended with exhaustion and grief. Many describe it as validating and clever.

books.title: Asking For It
books.author: Louise O'Neill
books.ratingNote: Strong international readership with heavy discussion.
reviewSummary: After a sexual assault goes public, a teen faces media scrutiny and community judgment. Readers praise the unflinching portrayal of victim-blaming. Reviews often describe the book as brutal but necessary. Many say it sparks important conversations about rape culture.

books.title: Like Home
books.author: Louisa Onome
books.ratingNote: Strong emotional engagement tied to community themes.
reviewSummary: A teen grapples with gentrification, media attention, and fractured friendships after violence hits her neighborhood. Readers praise the sense of place and moral complexity. Reviews often highlight community loyalty and loss. Many describe it as timely and grounded.

books.title: How You Grow Wings
books.author: Rimma Onoseta
books.ratingNote: Positive reception for its intensity and suspense.
reviewSummary: Two sisters escape an abusive home only to find safety and danger in unexpected forms. Readers praise the tension and moral ambiguity. Reviews often highlight themes of survival and agency. Many describe it as gripping and dark.

books.title: Nick and Charlie
books.author: Alice Oseman
books.ratingNote: Very strong fan-driven ratings.
reviewSummary: A novella exploring whether first love can survive long-distance. Readers praise the emotional honesty and familiar voices. Reviews often highlight anxiety and communication struggles. Many fans describe it as tender and reassuring.

books.title: Radio Silence
books.author: Alice Oseman
books.ratingNote: Consistently high ratings across platforms.
reviewSummary: A high-achieving student reconsiders her future after forming a deep friendship centered around a podcast. Readers praise the anti-burnout message and nuanced mental health portrayal. Reviews often highlight authenticity and quiet rebellion. Many describe it as life-changing.

books.title: I Was Born for This
books.author: Alice Oseman
books.ratingNote: Strong reader enthusiasm tied to fandom culture.
reviewSummary: Intertwining perspectives of a pop star and a devoted fan, the novel explores fame, anxiety, and belonging. Readers praise the honesty around fandom and mental health. Reviews often note how empathy drives the story. Many describe it as affirming and modern.

books.title: Solitaire
books.author: Alice Oseman
books.ratingNote: Mixed but thoughtful reader response.
reviewSummary: A cynical teen navigates loneliness, mental health, and unexpected connection. Readers praise the raw honesty and flawed protagonist. Reviews often mention its darker tone compared to Oseman’s later works. Many describe it as bleak but relatable.

books.title: Anger Is a Gift
books.author: Mark Oshiro
books.ratingNote: Strong classroom and discussion use.
reviewSummary: A teen confronts grief, panic attacks, and systemic injustice as school tensions rise. Readers praise the emotional urgency and political clarity. Reviews often highlight how anger is reframed as a catalyst for change. Many describe it as empowering.

books.title: Out Now: Queer We Go Again!
books.author: Saundra Mitchell (Editor)
books.ratingNote: Strong appreciation for its variety and representation.
reviewSummary: An anthology of queer YA stories ranging from realistic to fantastical. Readers praise the diversity of voices and tones. Reviews often highlight how accessible and joyful the collection feels. Many describe it as celebratory and inclusive.

books.title: What's Coming to Me
books.author: Francesca Padilla
books.ratingNote: Positive response to its mix of rage and resilience.
reviewSummary: A teen plots revenge against a predatory boss while dealing with grief and instability. Readers praise the catharsis and moral tension. Reviews often highlight anger as justified rather than destructive. Many describe it as gripping and emotionally satisfying.
